stem:
Aditya heats dry sugar crystals in the boiling tube shown in the diagram. Water droplets collect on the cooler upper wall, and a black solid remains at the bottom.

What does this show about sugar?

options.text: Sugar is a compound: heating decomposes it into carbon and water, so it contains more than one element.
Sugar is an element, because it began as one white solid in the tube.
The water droplets came from moist room air, not from the dry sugar.
Sugar was already a ready mixture of charcoal and water packed inside the crystals.

teacher.key_rationale: Heating dry sugar yields water and a black carbon residue, so sugar contains more than one element and is a compound. A single white look does not make it an element. Droplets come from the heated dry sugar, not from room air. Sugar is not a ready charcoal–water mixture before heating.
teacher.figure_note: Boiling tube with dry sugar, flame, upper water droplets, and black residue.
